text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Government decides to award state defence electronics group Thomson to Lagardere to create industrial group able to compete with world leaders. State will recapitalise Thomson for an expected 11 billion francs, Daewoo expects to take over subsidiary Thomson Multimedia. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).

-- Air France in commercial alliance with U.S. carriers Delta Airlines and Continental Airlines CALA.N, involves hub and flight code sharing, passenger exchanges. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
-- Civil servants, teachers, doctors, transport and other public sector workers strike against unemployment, for higher purchasing power and defence of public service.
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis rejects UDF party request to drop tax hikes on fuels and value added tax.
-- Compagnie de Suez returns to the black in the first half with profit of 772 million francs.
-- Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin supports labour unions call for strike.
-- European fund managers favour investing in Europe due to low long-term rates, survey shows.

-- Guy Wyser-Pratte, head of U.S. investment fund which has bought into Strafor Facom capital, spells out views on corporate governance, calls for independent audits, says seeks further investments in France.
-- Renault studies sale of wiring division to Sylea, a subsidiary of the Labinal group.
-- EU rejects German proposal to severely limit the circumstances in which European countries can run large budget deficits in the future.
-- Lagardere to take over Thomson, will create European heavyweight able of challenging the American market.
